title: Multi-speaker separation built for real conversations
summary: A recorded conversation has always been one track with everyone on it. Luel Multi-Speaker Separation gives each person back on their own. Trained on real conversations from our contributor network, now in closed beta.
body_markdown:
## Every voice in a conversation, on its own track


Think of every podcast, meeting, interview and call ever recorded. In almost all of them, the voices are stuck together. You can turn the whole thing up or down, but you can't lift one person out.


Now you can. Send a recording and each person comes back as their own clean track, from the first word to the last.


## Built on real conversations


Pulling voices apart in a short, clean clip is one thing. Real conversations are harder. People pause, laugh and change pace. One leans into the microphone while another sits back. And each voice has to stay on the same track for the whole hour, not just for ten seconds.


So we trained on real conversations. People in our contributor network record real conversations all over the world, talking the way people really talk. Our model learned from real people, in the real world.


Then we tested it on calls from people held out of training.


Those are real calls with three or four people each. Every person came back on their own track, and no one was swapped onto someone else's. The full results are on the[model page](https://www.luel.ai/lab/models/multi-speaker-separation) .


## Light on hardware


It runs on modest cloud GPUs at about the speed of the recording: an hour of audio takes about an hour. It handles two to four people and recordings up to 90 minutes. It works with audio up to 48 kHz and returns each track at the rate you sent.


Alongside the tracks you get a timeline of who talks when. Sounds the person tracks don't hold, like laughs and coughs, come back in a separate file marked as not a person.


## What it unlocks


Once every voice has its own track, a recording becomes something you can work with. Edit one voice without touching the others. Transcribe each speaker cleanly. Dub one person into another language. Study how people take turns. Turn hours of recorded conversation into data a model can learn from.


That is the bigger idea. The hardest data to find is real human behaviour, recorded well. Our contributor network collects it, and separation turns a messy recording into something usable.


## What comes next


This is a first release, and it is strongest when people take turns. Next we are working on crosstalk, shared-room microphones and more languages; most of our testing so far is in English. On some calls, up to about one long two-person call in four, it returns an extra track for a background sound or a piece of someone's speech, so listen to each track before you rely on it.


## Try it


Luel Multi-Speaker Separation is in closed beta.[Request access](https://www.luel.ai/request?model=multi-speaker-separation) and tell us what you are working with.
